title: Περιγράφοντας αλλαγές με το χρόνο / Describing changes over time
bridge: In Greek, describing changes over time often involves the use of the past imperfect tense (παρατατικός) to describe ongoing or habitual actions in the past, and the simple past tense (αόριστος) for completed actions. Unlike English, Greek does not use auxiliary verbs like 'used to' or 'would' for habitual past actions. Instead, the context and tense alone convey the meaning. Be cautious not to overuse the simple past tense when describing ongoing past actions, as this can sound unnatural in Greek.
rule: To describe changes over time in Greek, use the past imperfect tense (παρατατικός) for ongoing or repeated actions in the past, and the simple past tense (αόριστος) for completed actions. The past imperfect is formed by adding specific endings to the verb stem (e.g., -α, -ες, -ε, -αμε, -ατε, -αν for -ω verbs). The simple past tense often involves a more complex conjugation, with different endings and sometimes stem changes. For example, 'έγραφα' (I was writing) vs. 'έγραψα' (I wrote).

concept_examples.text: Όταν ήμουν μικρός, πήγαινα στο σχολείο με τα πόδια.
concept_examples.translation: When I was young, I used to go to school on foot.
concept_examples.phonetic: /oˈtan ˈimos miˈkɾos, piˈɣena sto sxiˈoli me ta ˈpoðia/

concept_examples.text: Πέρσι, έμαθα να μαγειρεύω ιταλική κουζίνα.
concept_examples.translation: Last year, I learned to cook Italian cuisine.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ˈperɣi, ˈeɱaθa na maɣiˈɾevο iˈtalici kuˈzina/

concept_examples.text: Τα καλοκαίρια, κολυμπούσαμε στη θάλασσα κάθε μέρα.
concept_examples.translation: In the summers, we used to swim in the sea every day.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ta kaɫoˈɣeɾia, koliˈβusame sti ˈθalasa ˈkaɣi ˈmera/

concept_examples.text: Χθες, άλλαξα τη γνώμη μου για το θέμα.
concept_examples.translation: Yesterday, I changed my mind about the topic.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ˈçtes, ˈalaksa ti ˈɣnomi mu ɣa to ˈθema/

common_error.wrong: Όταν ήμουν μικρός, έγραψα στο σχολείο κάθε μέρα.
common_error.correct: Όταν ήμουν μικρός, πήγαινα στο σχολείο κάθε μέρα.
common_error.explanation: English speakers often mistakenly use the simple past tense (αόριστος) for habitual actions in the past, which sounds unnatural in Greek. The past imperfect tense (παρατατικός) should be used instead to describe ongoing or repeated actions in the past.

examples.original: Κάθε πρωί, έτρωγα πρωινό με την οικογένειά μου.
examples.phonetic: /ˈkaθe proˈi, ˈetɾoɣa proiˈno me tin oikoɣeˈnʲa mu/
examples.translation: Every morning, I used to have breakfast with my family.
examples.note: Use the past imperfect tense to describe habitual actions in the past.

examples.original: Τα Σαββατοκύριακα, πηγαίναμε στο πάρκο.
examples.translation: On weekends, we used to go to the park.
examples.note: Notice how the verb 'πήγαινα' is conjugated in the past imperfect tense.

examples.original: Πέρσι, μετακόμισα σε νέα πόλη.
examples.translation: Last year, I moved to a new city.
examples.note: Use the simple past tense to describe a completed action in the past.

examples.original: Όταν με γνώρισες, δούλευα σε μια μικρή εταιρεία.
examples.phonetic: /oˈtan me ɣˈnɔɾises, ˈðuleva se mja ˈmikɾi eˈtɛɾia/
examples.translation: When you met me, I was working for a small company.
examples.note: Combine past imperfect and simple past tenses to describe overlapping actions.

examples.original: Τότε, διάβαζα περισσότερα βιβλία, αλλά τώρα βλέπω περισσότερες ταινίες.
examples.phonetic: /ˈtoto, ˈðiavaɾza peˈɾisota viˈɣlia, ˈala ˈtora ˈvlepo peˈɾisotes ˈtɛnjes/
examples.translation: Back then, I read more books, but now I watch more movies.
examples.note: Use the past imperfect tense to contrast past habits with present ones.

examples.original: Παλιά, δεν είχα κινητό, αλλά τώρα έχω δύο.
examples.phonetic: /paˈlja, ðen ˈiça ciˈnito, ˈala ˈtora ˈeço ˈðio/
examples.translation: In the past, I didn’t have a mobile phone, but now I have two.
examples.note: Highlight changes over time using contrasting sentences.

title: Εικασίες και Συμπεράσματα / Speculating and Making Deductions
bridge: In Greek, speculating and making deductions often involve the use of the subjunctive mood or conditional structures, which can be more explicit than in English. English speakers might rely on modal verbs like 'must' or 'might,' but Greek uses specific verb forms and particles like 'ίσως' (maybe) or 'μάλλον' (probably). Be cautious not to directly translate English modals, as Greek structures can be more nuanced.
rule: To speculate or make deductions in Greek, use the subjunctive mood with verbs like 'είναι' (to be) or 'έχω' (to have) in constructions such as 'ίσως να είναι...' (maybe it is...) or 'μάλλον έχει...' (probably he has...). For conditional deductions, use 'αν' (if) followed by the past tense, e.g., 'Αν ήταν εδώ, θα το ήξερε' (If he were here, he would know it). Avoid overusing 'ίσως' or 'μάλλον' in every sentence; context often dictates the level of certainty.

concept_examples.text: Ίσως να είναι στο σπίτι.
concept_examples.translation: Maybe he is at home.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ˈisɔs na ˈine stɔ ˈspiti/

concept_examples.text: Μάλλον έχει ξεχάσει το ραντεβού.
concept_examples.translation: Probably he has forgotten the appointment.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ˈmalon ˈeçi kseˈxasi tɔ randevu/

concept_examples.text: Αν ήταν εδώ, θα το ήξερε.
concept_examples.translation: If he were here, he would know it.
concept_examples.phonetic: /an ˈe.tan eˈðo, θa tɔ ˈikse.re/

concept_examples.text: Δε μπορεί, πρέπει να έχει φύγει.
concept_examples.translation: It can't be, he must have left.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ðe mboˈri, ˈprepi na ˈeçi ˈfi.ʝi/

common_error.explanation: English speakers often omit 'να' (to) after 'πρέπει' (must) when speculating, but Greek requires 'να' before the verb in the subjunctive mood. Always include 'να' after modal verbs like 'πρέπει' or 'μπορεί' (can) when making deductions.

examples.original: Ίσως να βρέξει σήμερα.
examples.translation: Maybe it will rain today.
examples.note: Use 'ίσως να' for simple speculations about future events.

examples.original: Μάλλον είναι άρρωστος.
examples.translation: Probably he is sick.
examples.note: Combine 'μάλλον' with the present tense for probable present states.

examples.original: Αν είχε χρόνο, θα ερχόταν.
examples.translation: If he had time, he would come.
examples.note: Use 'αν' with the past tense for conditional deductions.

examples.original: Δε μπορεί, έχει χάσει το λεωφορείο.
examples.translation: It can't be, he has missed the bus.
examples.note: Combine 'δε μπορεί' with a deduction for strong negative speculations.

examples.original: Ίσως να πήγε στο μαγαζί, αλλά δεν είμαι σίγουρος.
examples.phonetic: /ˈisɔs na ˈpɛʝe stɔ maɣaˈzi, ˈala ðen ˈime ˈsiɣuros/
examples.translation: Maybe he went to the store, but I'm not sure.
examples.note: Combine 'ίσως να' with additional clauses for complex speculations.

examples.original: Μάλλον θα έχει τελειώσει μέχρι τις οκτώ.
examples.phonetic: /ˈmalon θa ˈeçi teliˈɔsi ˈmeçi tis oˈʝo/
examples.translation: Probably he will have finished by eight.
examples.note: Use future perfect constructions for speculations about completed actions.

title: Εκφράζοντας Μεταμέλεια και Υποθετικές Καταστάσεις / Expressing Regret and Hypothetical Situations
bridge: In Greek, expressing regret often involves the use of the subjunctive mood with the particle 'να', which is quite different from English's reliance on 'wish' or 'if only'. Hypothetical situations are constructed with 'αν' (if), similar to English, but the word order and verb forms can be more flexible. Be cautious of overusing 'sorry' (συγνώμη) as it doesn’t always convey regret like in English; instead, Greeks often use phrases like 'λυπάμαι που' (I’m sorry that).
rule: To express regret, use the structure 'Λυπάμαι που + past tense' or 'Εύχομαι να + past subjunctive'. For hypothetical situations, use 'Αν + past tense' for unreal present or past conditions, and 'Αν + present tense' for real future possibilities. The subjunctive mood is formed with 'να + verb stem + ending' (e.g., να ήμουν, να πήγαινα). Remember, Greek often omits the subject pronoun, unlike English.

concept_examples.text: Λυπάμαι που δεν ήρθα στην πάρτι σου.
concept_examples.translation: I’m sorry that I didn’t come to your party.
concept_examples.phonetic: /liˈpame pu ðɛn ˈirθa stin ˈparti su/

concept_examples.text: Εύχομαι να είχα περισσότερα χρήματα.
concept_examples.translation: I wish I had more money.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ˈɛfçome na ˈiça peˈreo̞tera ˈçr̥imaˈta/

concept_examples.text: Αν είχα χρόνο, θα πήγαινα στο σινεμά.
concept_examples.translation: If I had time, I would go to the cinema.
concept_examples.phonetic: /an ˈiça ˈxrono θa ˈpiɣena sto sineˈma/

concept_examples.text: Αν έρθεις αύριο, θα σε δω.
concept_examples.translation: If you come tomorrow, I will see you.
concept_examples.phonetic: /an ˈerθis ˈavrio θa se ðo/

common_error.explanation: English speakers often use 'είμαι λυπημένος' (I am sad) instead of 'λυπάμαι' (I’m sorry) to express regret. While 'λυπημένος' describes an emotional state, 'λυπάμαι' directly conveys regret or apology, which is more appropriate in this context.

examples.original: Λυπάμαι που άργησα.
examples.translation: I’m sorry I was late.
examples.note: Use 'λυπάμαι που' + past tense to express regret for past actions.

examples.original: Εύχομαι να μην το είχα πει.
examples.translation: I wish I hadn’t said it.
examples.note: Use 'εύχομαι να' + past subjunctive for unreal past wishes.

examples.original: Αν είχα χρήματα, θα αγόραζα ένα αυτοκίνητο.
examples.phonetic: /an ˈiça ˈçr̥imaˈta θa aˈɣorazα ˈena aftoˈkinito/
examples.translation: If I had money, I would buy a car.
examples.note: Use 'αν' + past tense for unreal past conditions.

examples.original: Αν δεν έβρεχε, θα πηγαίναμε στην παραλία.
examples.phonetic: /an ðɛn ˈevreçe θa piɣeˈneme stin paˈralia/

examples.note: Combine 'αν' + past tense for unreal present or past situations.

examples.original: Αν έρθεις, θα σε δω.
examples.translation: If you come, I will see you.
examples.note: Use 'αν' + present tense for real future possibilities.

examples.original: Αν βρω χρόνο, θα σε καλέσω.
examples.translation: If I find time, I will call you.
examples.note: Combine 'αν' + present tense for real future conditions.

title: Πλεονεκτήματα και μειονεκτήματα / Advantages and Disadvantages
bridge: In Greek, discussing advantages and disadvantages often involves more explicit connectors than in English. While English uses 'pros and cons' or 'on the one hand... on the other hand,' Greek relies on phrases like 'από τη μία' and 'από την άλλη' to structure arguments. Be cautious with false friends like 'πλεονέκτημα' (advantage) and 'μειονέκτημα' (disadvantage), which are more formal than their English counterparts.
rule: To discuss advantages, use 'Ένα πλεονέκτημα είναι...' (One advantage is...) or 'Έχει πολλά οφέλη, όπως...' (It has many benefits, such as...). For disadvantages, use 'Ένα μειονέκτημα είναι...' (One disadvantage is...) or 'Υπάρχουν κάποιες δυσκολίες, όπως...' (There are some difficulties, such as...). Connectors like 'από τη μία' (on the one hand) and 'από την άλλη' (on the other hand) help structure balanced arguments. Avoid overusing 'αλλά' (but) as it can sound abrupt.

concept_examples.text: Ένα πλεονέκτημα του να ζεις στην πόλη είναι η εύκολη πρόσβαση σε υπηρεσίες.
concept_examples.translation: One advantage of living in the city is easy access to services.
concept_examples.phonetic: eˈna pleoˌne̞kˈtima tu na ˈzesis stin poˈli ine i ˈefkoli proˈsiɣi se iˈπiɾisme̞s

concept_examples.text: Ένα μειονέκτημα είναι η υψηλή ρύπανση.
concept_examples.translation: One disadvantage is the high pollution.
concept_examples.phonetic: eˈna mejoˌne̞kˈtima ine i iˈpsili ˈɾi̞paŋsi

concept_examples.text: Από τη μία, είναι βολικό, αλλά από την άλλη, είναι ακριβό.
concept_examples.translation: On the one hand, it's convenient, but on the other hand, it's expensive.
concept_examples.phonetic: aˈpo ti ˈmia, iˈne voˈliko, aˈla aˈpo tin aˈli, iˈne aˈkɾivo

concept_examples.text: Έχει πολλά οφέλη, όπως η κοινωνική ζωή, αλλά και κάποιες δυσκολίες.

concept_examples.phonetic: eˈçi poˈla oˈfeli, oˈse i koˈni̞tiki zoˈi, aˈla ke ˈɣapies ðisˈkolies

common_error.wrong: Είναι καλό γιατί είναι φθηνό, αλλά είναι κακό γιατί είναι θορυβώδες.
common_error.correct: Ένα πλεονέκτημα είναι ότι είναι φθηνό, αλλά ένα μειονέκτημα είναι ότι είναι θορυβώδες.
common_error.correct_alt: Από τη μία, είναι φθηνό, από την άλλη, είναι θορυβώδες.
common_error.explanation: English speakers often directly translate 'good' and 'bad' instead of using specific connectors like 'πλεονέκτημα' and 'μειονέκτημα.' Greek requires a more structured approach to discussing pros and cons, avoiding vague statements.

examples.original: Ένα πλεονέκτημα είναι...
examples.translation: One advantage is...
examples.note: Use this to introduce a pro.

examples.original: Ένα μειονέκτημα είναι...
examples.translation: One disadvantage is...
examples.note: Use this to introduce a con.

examples.original: Από τη μία...

examples.original: Από την άλλη...

examples.original: Έχει οφέλη, όπως..., αλλά και δυσκολίες, όπως...

examples.original: Αν και είναι βολικό, είναι ακριβό.
examples.phonetic: an ke iˈne voˈliko, iˈne aˈkɾivo
examples.translation: Although it's convenient, it's expensive.
examples.note: Use 'αν και' to concede a point.

title: Αφήγηση ιστορίας / Narrating a Story
bridge: In Greek, narrating a story involves using the imperfect tense (παρατατικός) to describe past actions, which is similar to the English past continuous. However, Greek often omits the subject pronoun when the context is clear, unlike English where subject pronouns are typically required. Additionally, Greek uses the particle 'και' (and) to connect events in a sequence, which is more frequent than in English.
rule: To narrate a story in Greek, use the imperfect tense (παρατατικός) for ongoing or repeated past actions. The imperfect is formed by adding specific endings to the verb stem: -α, -ες, -ε, -αμε, -ατε, -αν for -ω verbs (e.g., μιλούσα, μιλούσες). For -ώ verbs, the endings are -ούσα, -ούσες, -ούσε, -ούσαμε, -ούσατε, -ούσαν (e.g., έτρωγα, έτρωγες). Avoid overusing the simple past (αόριστος) unless describing completed actions. Use 'και' to link events, and omit subject pronouns when the context is clear.

common_error.explanation: English speakers often overuse subject pronouns in Greek. In Greek, subject pronouns are frequently omitted when the context is clear. Additionally, the incorrect example repeats 'εγώ,' which is redundant and unnatural in Greek.

examples.original: Κάθε μέρα, ξυπνούσα νωρίς.

title: Υποστηρίζω τη γνώμη μου / Arguing a Point of View
bridge: In Greek, arguing a point of view often involves more explicit use of modal verbs and expressions of certainty compared to English. While English speakers might rely on tone and context, Greek speakers tend to use phrases like 'πιστεύω ότι' (I believe that) or 'είμαι σίγουρος ότι' (I am sure that) to emphasize their stance. Be cautious not to overuse direct translations like 'I think' without the appropriate Greek structure, as it may sound less natural.
rule: To argue a point of view in Greek, use modal verbs such as 'πιστεύω' (I believe), 'νομίζω' (I think), and 'είμαι σίγουρος' (I am sure) followed by 'ότι' (that) and the main clause. Additionally, phrases like 'κατά τη γνώμη μου' (in my opinion) or 'από τη δική μου πλευρά' (from my side) can be used to introduce your perspective. Remember that Greek often requires more explicit expressions of certainty and opinion than English.

concept_examples.text: Πιστεύω ότι το κλίμα αλλάζει λόγω της ανθρώπινης δραστηριότητας.
concept_examples.translation: I believe that the climate is changing due to human activity.
concept_examples.phonetic: /piˈstevɔ ˈɔti to ˈklima aˈlaʝi ˈloɣu tis aˈnθrɔpinis ðraˈstiriɔtitas/

concept_examples.text: Νομίζω ότι πρέπει να λάβουμε μέτρα για την προστασία του περιβάλλοντος.

concept_examples.phonetic: /noˈmizo ˈɔti ˈprepi na ˈlavume ˈmetra ʝa tin proˈtasia tu perivˈɒndon/

concept_examples.text: Κατά τη γνώμη μου, η εκπαίδευση είναι το κλειδί για την πρόοδο.
concept_examples.translation: In my opinion, education is the key to progress.
concept_examples.phonetic: /kaˈta ti ˈɣnomi mu, i eɣiˈkiɒsi ˈine to kleˈði ʝa tin ˈprooðo/

concept_examples.text: Από τη δική μου πλευρά, πιστεύω ότι πρέπει να επενδύσουμε σε ανανεώσιμες πηγές ενέργειας.
concept_examples.translation: From my side, I believe we should invest in renewable energy sources.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aˈpo ti ðiˈki mu pleˈθra, piˈstevɔ ˈɔti ˈprepi na epeˈðisume se aɲaˈneɔsimes ˈpɪɣes eɲeˈrʝias/

common_error.correct: Πιστεύω ότι πρέπει να λάβουμε μέτρα για την προστασία του περιβάλλοντος.
common_error.correct_alt: Νομίζω ότι πρέπει να δράσουμε για το περιβάλλον.
common_error.explanation: English speakers often directly translate 'I think' or 'I believe' without using the appropriate Greek structure. While 'θεωρώ' (I consider) is correct, it is less commonly used in everyday arguments. Stick to 'πιστεύω' or 'νομίζω' for more natural expressions of opinion.

levels.label: Υποστηρίζω με επιχειρήματα / Supporting with Arguments

examples.original: Κατά τη γνώμη μου, η ανακύκλωση είναι απαραίτητη για το περιβάλλον.
examples.phonetic: /kaˈta ti ˈɣnomi mu, i aɲaˈkiklosi ˈine apaˈɾiti ti perivˈɒndon/
examples.translation: In my opinion, recycling is essential for the environment.
examples.note: Use 'κατά τη γνώμη μου' to introduce a reasoned argument.

examples.original: Από τη δική μου πλευρά, πιστεύω ότι η εκπαίδευση είναι το μέλλον.
examples.phonetic: /aˈpo ti ðiˈki mu pleˈθra, piˈstevɔ ˈɔti i eɣiˈkiɒsi ˈine to ˈmelon/
examples.translation: From my side, I believe that education is the future.
examples.note: Add 'από τη δική μου πλευρά' to emphasize your perspective.

levels.label: Απαντώ σε αντιρρήσεις / Responding to Counterarguments

examples.original: Καταλαβαίνω τη θέση σου, αλλά πιστεύω ότι υπάρχει λύση.
examples.phonetic: /kataɫaˈveno ti ˈθesi su, aˈla piˈstevɔ ˈɔti iˈparʝi ˈlisi/
examples.translation: I understand your point, but I believe there is a solution.
examples.note: Acknowledge the other's view with 'καταλαβαίνω τη θέση σου' before countering.

examples.original: Σέβομαι τη γνώμη σου, όμως νομίζω ότι πρέπει να εξετάσουμε άλλες επιλογές.
examples.phonetic: /ˈsevoɲe ti ˈɣnomi su, ˈomoɲ noˈmizo ˈɔti ˈprepi na eɣeˈtaʝume ˈaɫes epiˈloʝis/
examples.translation: I respect your opinion, but I think we should consider other options.
examples.note: Use 'σέβομαι τη γνώμη σου' to show respect while disagreeing.

title: Μιλώντας για τη δουλειά και την καριέρα / Talking about work and career
bridge: In Greek, discussing work and career often involves more formal expressions compared to English. For instance, Greeks frequently use the verb 'δουλεύω' (doulevo) for 'I work,' but 'εργάζομαι' (ergazomai) is more formal and common in professional settings. Be cautious with false friends like 'καριέρα' (kariera), which means 'career' but is used less frequently than in English, often replaced by 'επαγγελματική πορεία' (epaggelmatiki poria).
rule: To talk about work and career in Greek, use the present tense for current jobs and the past tense for past experiences. The verb 'είμαι' (ime) is used for professions, e.g., 'είμαι δάσκαλος' (ime daskalos - I am a teacher). For career progression, use phrases like 'προάγομαι' (proagomai - I get promoted) or 'αλλάζω δουλειά' (allazo douleia - I change jobs). Adjectives follow nouns, e.g., 'καλή δουλειά' (kali douleia - good job).

concept_examples.text: Δουλεύω ως μηχανικός σε μια μεγάλη εταιρεία.
concept_examples.translation: I work as an engineer in a large company.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ðuˈlevo os miçaniˈkos se mia ˈmeɣali etaiˈria/

concept_examples.text: Θέλω να κάνω καριέρα στον τομέα της τεχνολογίας.
concept_examples.translation: I want to make a career in the technology sector.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ˈθelo na ˈkano kaˈrjera ston toˈmea tis teçnoɣoˈɣias/

concept_examples.text: Προάχθηκα σε διευθυντική θέση πέρυσι.
concept_examples.translation: I was promoted to a managerial position last year.
concept_examples.phonetic: /proˈaθtika se ðiɣoɲtiˈki ˈθesi ˈperisi/

concept_examples.text: Αλλάζω δουλειά γιατί θέλω νέες προκλήσεις.
concept_examples.translation: I’m changing jobs because I want new challenges.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aˈlaʒo ˈðuleja ɣiˈati ˈθelo ˈnees proˈklisis/

common_error.wrong: Είμαι καριέρα στον τομέα της τεχνολογίας.
common_error.correct: Κάνω καριέρα στον τομέα της τεχνολογίας.
common_error.explanation: English speakers often misuse 'είμαι' (I am) with 'καριέρα' (career) due to the English structure 'I am in a career.' In Greek, 'κάνω καριέρα' (I make a career) is the correct phrase. 'Είμαι' is used for professions, not career paths.

examples.original: Είμαι δικηγόρος.
examples.translation: I am a lawyer.
examples.note: Use 'είμαι' (I am) followed by the profession.

examples.original: Δουλεύω ως γιατρός.
examples.translation: I work as a doctor.
examples.note: Use 'δουλεύω ως' (I work as) for current roles.

examples.original: Ξεκίνησα ως βοηθός και τώρα είμαι διευθυντής.
examples.phonetic: /kseˈkinisa os voˈðos ki ˈtora iˈme ðiɣoɲˈtis/
examples.translation: I started as an assistant and now I am a manager.
examples.note: Use past tense for starting positions and present for current roles.

examples.original: Θέλω να προάγω στην εταιρεία.
examples.translation: I want to get promoted in the company.
examples.note: Use 'προάγω' (I get promoted) for career advancement.

examples.original: Αλλάζω τομέα γιατί θέλω νέες ευκαιρίες.
examples.translation: I’m changing fields because I want new opportunities.
examples.note: Use 'αλλάζω' (I change) for shifting careers or fields.

examples.original: Αποφάσισα να κάνω μια νέα αρχή.
examples.translation: I decided to make a fresh start.
examples.note: Use 'κάνω μια νέα αρχή' (I make a fresh start) for significant changes.

title: Πώς λειτουργεί / How it works
bridge: In Greek, describing processes often involves the use of the present tense with the particle 'πώς' (how) to explain steps or mechanisms. Unlike English, Greek does not rely heavily on phrasal verbs like 'work out' or 'carry out' for process descriptions. Instead, it uses simple verb forms and prepositions like 'με' (with) or 'χωρίς' (without) to indicate means or conditions. Be cautious not to overuse the English equivalent of 'then' or 'after that'; Greek often omits explicit sequencing words, relying on verb order instead.
rule: To describe processes in Greek at the B1 level, use the present tense with the particle 'πώς' to introduce the explanation. Follow this with a series of verbs in the present tense to describe each step. Use prepositions like 'με' (with), 'χωρίς' (without), or 'μέσω' (via) to indicate tools or methods. Avoid complex tenses or passive voice; stick to active voice and simple sentence structures. Sequencing can be implied through verb order, but adverbs like 'πρώτα' (first), 'μετά' (after), or 'τέλος' (finally) can be added for clarity.

concept_examples.text: Πώς λειτουργεί το μηχάνημα; Βάζεις το κέρμα, πατάς το κουμπί, και παίρνεις το εισιτήριο.
concept_examples.translation: How does the machine work? You insert the coin, press the button, and get the ticket.
concept_examples.phonetic: /pos liɣoˈniɣi to miˈxaniɣma? vaˈziz to ˈkermi, paˈtas to kuˈbi, e piˈɾnis to iˈsitirio/

concept_examples.text: Για να φτιάξεις αυτή τη συνταγή, πρώτα πλένεις τα λαχανικά, μετά τα κόβεις, και τέλος τα μαγειρεύεις.
concept_examples.translation: To make this recipe, first you wash the vegetables, then you cut them, and finally you cook them.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ˈʝa na fˈtʝaks afˈti ti sinˈdaʝi, ˈproto ˈplenis ta laxaniˈka, ˈmeta ta ˈkovis, e ˈtelos ta maʝiˈreviz/

concept_examples.text: Το σύστημα λειτουργεί με ηλιακή ενέργεια: απορροφά την ηλιακή ακτινοβολία και τη μετατρέπει σε ηλεκτρισμό.
concept_examples.translation: The system works with solar energy: it absorbs solar radiation and converts it into electricity.
concept_examples.phonetic: /to sisˈtima liɣoˈniɣi me iˈljakʲi eˈneɾʝia: apoɾoˈfa tin iˈljakʲi aktiɾoβoˈlia e ti metaˈtɾepi se elekˈtɾismo/

concept_examples.text: Για να ανοίξεις τον λογαριασμό, χρειάζεσαι ταυτότητα, συμπληρώνεις τη φόρμα, και περιμένεις την επιβεβαίωση.
concept_examples.translation: To open the account, you need an ID, fill out the form, and wait for confirmation.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ˈʝa na aˈniʝis ton loɣaˈrʝasmos, xɾiˈazese taˈfotita, simpliˈɾonis ti ˈfoɾma, e peɾiˈmenis tin epiβeˈveosi/

common_error.wrong: Πώς λειτουργεί το μηχάνημα; Μετά βάζεις το κέρμα, μετά πατάς το κουμπί, και μετά παίρνεις το εισιτήριο.
common_error.correct: Πώς λειτουργεί το μηχάνημα; Βάζεις το κέρμα, πατάς το κουμπί, και παίρνεις το εισιτήριο.
common_error.explanation: English speakers often overuse sequencing words like 'μετά' (then) in Greek, which sounds unnatural. Greek relies on verb order to imply sequence, so explicit sequencing words are usually unnecessary unless emphasizing a specific order.

examples.original: Πρώτα βάζεις το νερό, μετά προσθέτεις το αλάτι.
examples.phonetic: /ˈproto ˈvazis to neˈɾo, ˈmeta proˈstetis to aˈlati/
examples.translation: First you add the water, then you add the salt.
examples.note: Use 'πρώτα' and 'μετά' to sequence simple actions.

examples.original: Ανοίγεις την πόρτα, μπαίνεις μέσα, και κλείνεις την πόρτα.
examples.phonetic: /aˈniʝis tin ˈporta, ˈbenis ˈmesa, e ˈklinis tin ˈporta/
examples.translation: You open the door, enter, and close the door.
examples.note: Verb order implies sequence without explicit markers.

examples.original: Φτιάχνεις καφέ με βραστό νερό και καφετιέρα.
examples.phonetic: /fˈtʝaxnis kaˈfe me ˈvɾasto neˈɾo e kafetiˈeɾa/
examples.translation: You make coffee with boiling water and a coffee maker.
examples.note: Use 'με' (with) to indicate tools or ingredients.

examples.original: Μαθαίνεις ελληνικά χωρίς δάσκαλο.
examples.translation: You learn Greek without a teacher.
examples.note: Use 'χωρίς' (without) to indicate absence of means.

examples.original: Ακολουθώντας αυτές τις οδηγίες, θα έχεις ένα τέλειο αποτέλεσμα.
examples.phonetic: /akoloˈθondas afˈtes tis oðiˈʝis, θa ˈexis eˈna ˈtεlio apoˈtεlεsma/
examples.translation: Following these instructions, you’ll have a perfect result.
examples.note: Use 'ακολουθώντας' (following) to link process to outcome.

examples.original: Με αυτή τη μέθοδο, εξοικονομείς χρόνο και ενέργεια.
examples.phonetic: /me ˈafti ti ˈmeðoðo, eksiciˈnomis ˈxrono e eˈneɾʝia/
examples.translation: With this method, you save time and energy.
examples.note: Use 'με' (with) to introduce the method and its benefits.

title: Εκφράζοντας Αβεβαιότητα / Expressing Uncertainty
bridge: In Greek, expressing uncertainty often involves modal verbs and adverbs similar to English, but the structure can differ. For instance, Greek uses 'ίσως' (maybe) and 'πιθανόν' (probably) more frequently than English relies on 'might' or 'could'. Be cautious with word order, as Greek often places adverbs of uncertainty after the verb, unlike English. Additionally, Greek speakers tend to use the subjunctive mood more explicitly in certain contexts, which English often implies without a specific marker.
rule: To express uncertainty in Greek, use adverbs like 'ίσως' (maybe), 'πιθανόν' (probably), or 'ίσως όχι' (maybe not). Modal verbs such as 'μπορεί να' (might) or 'ίσως να' (may) are also common. The subjunctive mood is often used after expressions of uncertainty, e.g., 'Νομίζω ότι ίσως έρθει' (I think he might come). Word order is flexible but typically follows the pattern: Subject + Verb + Adverb of Uncertainty. Exceptions include questions, where the adverb may appear earlier for emphasis.

concept_examples.text: Ίσως πάω στο σινεμά απόψε.
concept_examples.translation: I might go to the cinema tonight.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ˈisɔs ˈpɔ ʝe sto sineˈma aˈpɔpsɛ/

concept_examples.text: Πιθανόν να βρέξει αύριο.
concept_examples.translation: It’s probably going to rain tomorrow.
concept_examples.phonetic: /piθaˈnon na ˈvɾɛksi ˈavɾio/

concept_examples.text: Δεν είμαι σίγουρος αν θα έρθει.
concept_examples.translation: I’m not sure if he will come.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ðɛn ˈime ˈsiɣuros an θa ˈɛɾθi/

concept_examples.text: Μπορεί να έχει δίκιο.
concept_examples.translation: She might be right.
concept_examples.phonetic: /boˈɾi na ˈeçi ˈðikio/

common_error.explanation: English speakers often incorrectly use 'θα' (will) after 'ίσως' (maybe), which is redundant in Greek. 'Ίσως' already implies uncertainty, so adding 'θα' is unnecessary and sounds unnatural. Stick to 'ίσως + verb' for correct usage.

examples.original: Ίσως να έρθει.
examples.translation: He might come.
examples.note: Use 'ίσως να' for simple uncertainty.

examples.original: Πιθανόν να βρέξει.
examples.translation: It’s probably going to rain.
examples.note: Combine 'πιθανόν να' with a verb for probability.

examples.original: Μπορεί να έρθεις;
examples.translation: Might you come?
examples.note: Use 'μπορεί να' in questions for polite uncertainty.

examples.original: Ίσως να έχεις δίκιο;
examples.translation: Might you be right?
examples.note: Add 'να' after 'ίσως' in questions for emphasis.

examples.original: Νομίζω ότι ίσως να έρθει.
examples.translation: I think he might come.
examples.note: Combine 'νομίζω ότι' with 'ίσως να' for layered uncertainty.

examples.original: Αν ίσως βρέξει, θα μείνουμε σπίτι.
examples.translation: If it might rain, we’ll stay home.
examples.note: Use 'αν ίσως' in conditional sentences for hypothetical uncertainty.

title: Κάντε επίσημες αιτήσεις / Making Formal Requests
bridge: In Greek, formal requests often use the subjunctive mood with the particle 'να', which is quite different from English's direct use of 'can' or 'could'. Greek also emphasizes politeness through specific verb forms and expressions, unlike English where tone and context play a larger role. Be cautious not to overuse the informal 'θέλω' (I want) in formal settings, as it can sound too direct.
rule: To make formal requests in Greek, use the subjunctive mood with 'να' followed by the verb in the first person singular. For example, 'Να κάνω...' (May I do...). Additionally, phrases like 'Παρακαλώ' (Please) and 'Μπορώ να...' (Can I...) are common. Always use the polite form of address, such as 'κυρία' (Mrs.) or 'κύριε' (Mr.), when addressing someone formally. Exceptions include situations where a closer relationship is established, but for B1 level, stick to formal structures.

concept_examples.text: Μπορώ να κάνω μια ερώτηση;
concept_examples.translation: Can I ask a question?
concept_examples.phonetic: /boˈro na ˈkano miɲ eˈrɔtisi/

concept_examples.text: Παρακαλώ, να κλείσω το παράθυρο;
concept_examples.translation: Please, may I close the window?
concept_examples.phonetic: /paˈraɣo na ˈkliso to paˈraθiro/

concept_examples.text: Να σας ρωτήσω κάτι, κύριε;
concept_examples.translation: May I ask you something, sir?
concept_examples.phonetic: /na sas roˈtiso ˈkati, ˈkirie/

concept_examples.text: Θα ήθελα να ζητήσω μια πληροφορία.
concept_examples.translation: I would like to request some information.
concept_examples.phonetic: /θa ˈiθela na ziˈtiso miɲ pliropiˈria/

common_error.explanation: Using 'θέλω' (I want) in formal requests can sound too direct and impolite. Instead, use 'μπορώ' (can I) or 'παρακαλώ' (please) with the subjunctive mood to maintain formality and politeness.

examples.original: Μπορώ να πάω στην τουαλέτα;
examples.translation: Can I go to the bathroom?
examples.note: Use 'μπορώ' for simple, polite requests.

examples.original: Παρακαλώ, να καθίσω εδώ;
examples.translation: Please, may I sit here?
examples.note: Add 'παρακαλώ' for extra politeness.

examples.original: Μπορώ να ανοίξω το παράθυρο γιατί κάνει ζέστη;
examples.phonetic: /boˈro na aˈniκso to paˈraθiro ɣiˈati ˈkani ˈzesti/
examples.translation: Can I open the window because it's hot?
examples.note: Add 'γιατί' to explain the reason for the request.

examples.original: Να σας ρωτήσω γιατί καθυστερεί το λεωφορείο;
examples.phonetic: /na sas roˈtiso ɣiˈati kaθisteˈri to levoˈreo/
examples.translation: May I ask you why the bus is delayed?
examples.note: Use 'να σας ρωτήσω' for formal inquiries.

examples.original: Θα ήθελα να ζητήσω μια επέκταση της προθεσμίας.
examples.phonetic: /θa ˈiθela na ziˈtiso miɲ eˈpitaɲi tis proθesˈmias/
examples.translation: I would like to request an extension of the deadline.
examples.note: Use 'θα ήθελα να ζητήσω' for more formal, complex requests.

examples.original: Μπορώ να σας παρακαλέσω να ελέγξετε την κράτηση μου;
examples.phonetic: /boˈro na sas paˈrakalo na eˈleκste tin ˈkratisi mu/
examples.translation: Can I ask you to check my reservation?
examples.note: Combine 'μπορώ' with 'να σας παρακαλέσω' for added politeness.
